adjustedAfterLooking.why: punchIn.scale: I measured the punched frames against the wide at 0:06.233, using the white shelf cubes (their width and the gap between them), not Ben's head, because he leans. Readings: 0:48.667 and 1:07.833 about 1.17, 1:17.433 about 1.25, 1:34.633 and 1:50.767 about 1.3, 0:26.133 about 1.38 (median about 1.27). Many punched shots then keep pushing in by 0.1-0.2, and there is a separate tight gag level of about 1.5 (0:05.300); a static 1.25 is the middle of the normal punch range. cutRate: all 24 checked detections are real picture changes, but only 16 are host framing jump cuts. The rest are clip entries/exits (3), cuts inside a reacted clip's own montage (3), the elephant graphic (1) and the file's first frame (1), so 8.06 x 16/24 gives about 5.4 per minute over the runtime. That is about 9 per minute inside host-only stretches (16 in 104 s) and none while a clip is up. In the first 60 s, 8 of the 12 detections are host framing changes. captions (null = not set before, so the build-timeline default of 42 characters and 5 s applied): the reference shows 1-4 word cues, the longest seen 25 characters, with a new cue about every second (every 1 fps tile in the first minute has a different caption).
